messages.text: Hi there — I'm Sarah, an AI researcher with HeliumDeploy. Thank you so much for taking 25 minutes to do this — it really means a lot. Honestly, the more you can share with me, the better — we're aiming for about fifteen hundred words of feedback together, so please don't worry about going long. The founders read every word of these chats, so what you say actually shapes what HD does next. As a thank-you you'll get a $75 discount code at the end. So — to kick us off, tell me about your mining setup right now. What are you running, where, and what are you trying to figure out next?

I'm running a power mining dot IO one terahash per second. Uh, mining rig I got off Amazon. Just to see how it went. I got it set up. It's been running for a few days. And I've been happy with it and would like to go up to something between four and six terahash.

Got it — you've got the 1 TH/s Power Mining unit off Amazon running, a few days in, and now you're eyeing something in the 4–6 TH/s range. Makes sense.

Let me pull up the one I'm guessing caught your eye — Have you seen this one — the NerdQaxe Rev 6.1?
That that is correct. That's the one I've been eyeballing
Nice — that's the one. What did you think of it?
Looks like a pretty good unit. Especially for the cost right now with you guys running it on sale.
Good catch on the sale. So — you've got the 1 TH/s Power Mining unit running. Why jump to 6 TH/s next, rather than say, adding another small one or going way bigger?
I'm looking at it from a cost per perspective of cost per what I'm mining, I guess. And this one being on sale, if it wasn't on sale, I'd be looking at the nerd Octax.

Interesting — so the sale on the NerdQaxe is what's pulling you in, but if it were full price, you'd jump up to the NerdOctaxe. Walk me through that math — what's the cost-per number that you're actually running in your head?

Well, when I'm looking at six point one or six terahash per second for two hundred and fifty bucks versus five hundred to six hundred depending on the vendor for ten. Uh, you know, nine point four. That's where I'm looking at the number. Um, and also not only that, but the what I'm looking at is what the wattage is for what you're getting per terahash.

Okay — so two levers: dollars per TH, and watts per TH. Smart. 

Walk me through the watts side — what number are you targeting, and what are you running today on the Power Mining unit?

I don't have a number. I'm an electrician by trade, so I know when I look at for example, my power mining IO one, it's fifteen, eighteen watts per one terahash. That's not very much. When you look at this one, I believe these are around a hundred watts for about six. Versus I don't know if they're older models or what or however they're overclocked probably. Because they've got better cooling and and that kind of stuff why they can run higher. But um, when you're looking about six terahash per hundred watts versus jumping up to the nine, which from what I've seen, they can run up to twelve, I'm guessing, again, all because of the cooling that they have. Uh, they're running around three I think it's two to three hundred watts So that's what I'm looking at to me. And it'd almost be worth getting two of these right around two hundred watts versus those in real world. They're I think, two hundred watts plus. So I

Got it — and the fact that you're an electrician by trade means you're actually reading the spec sheet like a spec sheet, not marketing copy. That's rare.

So here's a push-back — at 6 TH for ~100W you're at roughly 16 W/TH, which is basically identical to your Power Mining 1 TH at 15–18 W/TH. You wouldn't actually be gaining efficiency, just hashrate. Is that the trade you're making consciously — pay for more hashrate at the same efficiency — or were you hoping the bigger unit would also be more efficient per terahash?

No. I'm looking at it, and that that may work out that way. But when I'm looking at this, at six terahash, the unit I just bought from Power Mining was about on sale, ninety nine bucks. So I'd have to buy five more of those. So we're talking five hundred dollars. And, yes, the wattage may be the same, but it also comes out in that price for the unit as well.

Oh — that's the real math. Six of the little ones is $500 and a power-strip nightmare; one NerdQaxe is $249 for the same hashrate. Got it.

So when you set up the Power Mining unit a few days ago — what was that experience like? Did it just plug in and go, or did you have to mess with pools, wallet addresses, firmware, anything like that?

Not really. I as being a navy new ex Navy guy, I did my homework and spent about, I don't know, six to eight hours watching videos. It was pretty easy to set up. Considering I've, you know, built computers before and uh, set this unit up. But the the big thing was we're the only holdup was me not paying attention to the screen because it is a smaller screen. Not seeing that the last digit was a eight and not a dot zero, and that's what held me up for about two minutes other than that. Already had it lined up and decided that until I get more terahashash per second, I wasn't actually gonna try to mine Bitcoin. I mean, the odds are still astronomical, but I decided to do uh, solo mining for Bitcoin Cash because ultimately, that's still probably a higher probability even though it's still a long shot to hit. A one of those, and it would be for Bitcoin right now until I, you know, I'd figure at least get ten twelve, fourteen terahash per second before I venture over to the Bitcoin side. In a solo mine pool.

That is a really thoughtful strategy — going Bitcoin Cash solo first because the odds are at least *less* astronomical, then graduating to Bitcoin once you've got 10–14 TH stacked. I haven't heard that one before from anybody I've talked to.

So tell me more about the endgame — what does 10-14 TH look like for you? Is it just stacking NerdQaxes one at a time, or something else?

I don't know. To be honest with you, I thought when I bought the first one, uh, you know, the, uh, the gamma six zero two is what I have. I'd like to next progressively go to a Nerd QX and then possibly go to an Octax and look at it from there. Um, it gets to a point where the Octax is a pretty big unit where these I mean, again, probably two of these units are the equivalent, but to start with, it's a direction to go.

Got it — so the path is Gamma → NerdQaxe → Octaxe, climbing the ladder one step at a time. 

You mentioned the Octaxe gets "pretty big." Where are these things actually living in your house right now — and where would the Octaxe go if you got there?

Honestly, I don't know the, uh, the gammas by my TV and my master. Uh, I'd have to look at some room. And obviously, if I get to a certain point where there's quite a few of these things, they may have to go live in my garage. Part of why I don't really wanna jump up to, like, a ant miner and stuff like that because you're talking much bigger units and starting to have to build racking and all that kind stuff. That's why I wanna see you know, get at least a couple of these and see where it goes.
Master bedroom, next to the TV — that's wild. Most people I talk to are hiding these things in basements. So the noise on the Gamma isn't bothering you?

No. Not me. I actually slightly overclocked it, and it wasn't bad, but decided since I had moved it when I set it up at work uh, brought it home. And it was I won't say noisy. It's still pretty quiet for what it is, but I dropped it back to a stock setting. And that for me, I can barely hear it. My wife under their hand, different story.

Ha — there it is. So the Gamma went from your work setup to the bedroom, you overclocked it, then dialed it back to stock because your wife could hear it. That's the real story.

Tell me about the overclock — what were you running it at, and how'd you decide what to push it to?

Well, I went conservative. I know a little bit about overclocking. I've messed with, uh, PCs, and usually, I don't mess with them. I I've I've four enough to have a fancy motherboard that let me auto overclock it, but this thing, I literally went one step up on the frequency and the voltage, and it was very stable. And bumped it up to almost one point two terahash a second. And to me, the gain wasn't that noticed for going from fifteen to seventeen watts, which again in the cost. And, um, decided just for quietness to bump it back to what the factory setting was.

Gotcha — so one notch up on frequency and voltage, picked up ~0.2 TH, but the extra watts + noise didn't justify it for a bedroom unit. Smart restraint.

Where'd you actually learn the overclock procedure — was that the 6–8 hours of YouTube before

No. I just when you look at it, this is not to be mean. This is pretty basic unless you have zero computer understanding. I literally bumped it up one notch for frequency and one notch notch for voltage when there are multiple steps I could go. Plus even if I would have continued to overclock it, I would have just done it step at a time, watched it to see what the temperature was running on the ASIC chip and how it was responding, also looking at again, if you're looking at trying to be efficient, looking at the watt usage. Again, it may not be quite real real world because it's what the the OS axe OS is showing. Uh, I don't per se have something to plug it into to see the the actual usage. Because if I really wanted to do it, I don't even know if I trust one of the wall plug in units. I'd go grab my clamp on amp meter and figure out what the phase is actually pulling.

Right — and as an electrician you've got the clamp meter sitting in the truck anyway. Of course.

So you're running AxeOS stock, you've got the clamp meter handy, and you're climbing the ladder. Are you in any of the Discords or subreddits where people swap overclock profiles and firmware tips — or are you mostly figuring this out solo?

No. I'm doing it so and to be honest with you, I I don't wanna overclock something because to be honest with you, I'd rather not and have it run stable and not take a chance of degrading lifetime because that's what people don't look at. Yeah. You might get some more terahash per second, but what are you doing to the unit and its overall life? I'd rather have something last longer than I would because, again, the odds are astronomical that you're gonna hit something I'd rather have it run longer at a slower speed than to run faster and last not nearly as long. And then I've gotta buy another unit. So

Yeah — that's a really different philosophy from a lot of the tinkerers I talk to who push hard for the squeeze. You're optimizing for *unit lifetime* as part of the cost equation. The miner is a depreciating asset and you don't want to accelerate that.

So — when you were doing the 6-8 hours of YouTube homework before buying the Gamma, where did you actually land? Whose videos were you watching?

There were a few videos I watched. It was mainly, uh, not so much after I kinda decided I was gonna go with a gamma it was more about setting up a wallet because I didn't have a crypto wallet and then figuring out where to go pool and mining. And I'm still not a hundred percent. I just found one that had for Bitcoin Cash that had a low tier for, you know, more simpler hardware versus a medium and a high. Versus just an overall pool solo pool to go into. So that's kinda and I think the guy's name might be Red Fox or something. It's got a Fox on the screen I watched him and somebody else, but that's neither her nor there. Uh, I'm pretty good with hearing what people's information is and deciding whether it's pushing a product or giving you true information.
Got it — Red Panda Mining maybe? Lot of folks find us through that channel and a couple others on YouTube.
Yep. Yeah. That's actually where I think I found this was through red Panda mining.

Yeah, that tracks — Red Panda sends a lot of folks our way.

So let me pivot — since you're an electrician and you're already thinking about wattage, phases, clamp meters — how are these miners actually wired up at your place? Are they on Wi-Fi, or did you run Ethernet to them?

No. The the the first unit I got, of course, I'm only running one. It is it's, uh, power mining dot I o. It's it is set up for Wi Fi, and it's seems to be fine. Even in my bedroom setup. Um, I don't really have a setup to unfortunately, my house isn't rigged up with Ethernet, or that would probably be the ideal connection and I'm not gonna go digging through the walls to start running a bunch of Ethernet cable.

Yeah, fair — Wi-Fi's fine until it isn't, and tearing into walls is a hard no.

Let me show you something we're researching — A small Ethernet adapter, around $34.99, that snaps onto the miner so you can run wired instead of Wi-Fi. Is that something you'd actually use, given your setup?

Probably not because where my modem router is. I don't you know, I'd I'd just not a good place to set it up. Plus, I'd rather have a have more airflow than stuff it behind my TV. I've already got a media server running behind it, and I don't wanna add too much more heat because there's not great airflow back there.

Yep — heat behind the TV is real, and you've already got the media server doing its thing back there. Makes sense.

Speaking of multiple devices generating heat — you mentioned summer. (address hidden) isn't exactly Phoenix, but does the season factor in at all when you think about adding a 100W NerdQaxe to the bedroom?
No. I've got AC in the house, and it's stays I keep my house about sixty nine to seventy degrees.

Perfect — climate's a non-issue then.

Okay so let me zoom out. You filled out a research popup on our site about an hour into looking at the NerdQaxe — what made you stop and fill that out? Most people don't.

Well, I'm not gonna lie to you. The the thing being on sale for two forty nine and another seventy five bucks off makes it on top of already being one of the cheapest, even cheaper. And with shipping, makes it right around a hundred and eighty, two hundred bucks which is, to me, worth giving a shot. If not, I would just wait till somebody ran on a cell because I'm not again, not in a hurry, but I recognize cost per value versus waiting. So I I don't mind having another unit let it run.

Smart — and honest. So the $75 discount code is genuinely moving the needle for you, not just a nice-to-have.

Let me ask the harder question — if this discount weren't on the table, what would you actually do? Wait for the next sale, or buy a second Power Mining unit off Amazon at $99 to bridge the gap?

I would probably just wait till something that sparked my was ran on sale that I thought would be worth adding. Again, not in a hurry, but for this being on sale and having another discount makes it very much worth looking at.

Got it — so you're not desperate, you're opportunistic. The stacked discount is what flips this from "watching" to "buying."

Quick one — when you were comparing the NerdQaxe to the Octaxe earlier, did you use anything specific to compare them side by side? A spreadsheet, ASIC Miner Value, our site, a YouTube comparison?

No. I've I've used lots of things between looking at the specs, the YouTube videos on it, and for right now the cost. That's the big breaker because um, again, I gotta get started somewhere. When you look at a hundred dollars for the power mining, that's actually this would have been the the smart thing to start with. But I wanted to get one up and running and see how it worked, how easy it was to set up, and basically put your feet in the water. And then to me, with the cost, this is the net next logical step. If this wasn't potentially at two hundred or less, yeah, it would to me, it would be worth just going straight to an OctaX.

Got it. Let me show you something — There's a comparison table on our homepage that lays the four miners out side by side — Gamma, NerdQaxe, Octaxe, Nexus S1. Did you scroll down to this one when you were on the site, or did you head straight to the NerdQaxe product page?

No. It popped up. I've looked at both of them, but I didn't see two ninety nine as a price. Point because then that might be even more me looking at it for the hundred and forty watt because you need at least two of these to make that one. And, again, for your wattage and what you're getting, that would be the smarter one. But when I looked, it was only four ninety nine and not two ninety nine for the nerd oct ax.

Wait — you're seeing $299 on the Octaxe in that table? Let me look... yeah, that's the sale price showing there. If that's real, that completely changes your math — 9.4 TH at 140W for $299 vs the NerdQaxe at 6 TH for $249. The O. is actually the better deal on both axes.

Is that going to make you pause and reconsider, or are you still leaning NerdQaxe?
Not to be to be honest with you, for two ninety nine, that's a different price than what it showed. Yeah. I'd be at that.

Yeah — that's a genuine surprise then. So the pricing on the comparison table might actually be steering you toward a different SKU than the one you were locked in on. Good signal for us.

Let me ask — when you opened our site originally and landed on the NerdQaxe page directly, where did the $299 Octaxe price NOT show up that should have? Was it not visible on the Octaxe product page itself, or did you just not click through to it?

Well, it could be possible because there's sometimes of these units, there's multiple ones, but I could've swore when I went to the nerd, Octax, it was normally, I think, five ninety nine on sale for four ninety nine, still not a bad price in comparison to the other ones. But it was definitely not showing two ninety nine now, whether that went on sale today or the last time I checked, I think, was yesterday. Uh, I was kept looking at the QX, and maybe this went on sale in the meantime.

Could be — sales rotate. But that's actually really useful for us to know: someone who's done his homework, who is *actively* shopping, sees a $200 swing between two visits and that's enough to change the SKU he buys. Pricing volatility matters.

So practically — are you going to go look at the Octaxe page right now after we hang up, or has this conversation tipped you toward pulling the trigger on it tonight?
I'm gonna go probably look at the aux tax. And if it's truly two ninety nine and the seventy five dollar discount adds, to it, then, yeah, I'll probably go to that and just skip the QX.

That's a real outcome from this call then — appreciate you being straight with me about it.

Last thing I want to ask — when you eventually do hit your 10-14 TH target and switch over to solo Bitcoin mining, do you see yourself going beyond that? Like, is there a vision where you're running a small farm in the garage, or is the goal more "I've got enough hashrate to play the lottery and I'm done"?

No. I think for now, I'll probably play the lottery because I really don't wanna be running three thousand four five thousand watt machines in the garage and cranking out heat like nobody's business These are much smaller even if you get several of these. You're it's gonna take quite a few before you hit the three thousand watt mark. Plus, it makes it easier even if I wanna put one here and one there. Not running like an Antminer s nineteen or twenty one. And there are these big boxes, which I don't really care what they look like. They're still doing the same thing. But is kinda nice to have these newer units that are kinda pleasant to look at because ultimately, the odds of striking are zero But on the off chance that you do, it's not nearly as bad getting a let's say, four or five hundred or even a few you know, close to a thousand tied up in these versus you're starting to buy units at two thousand a piece, and you you still might not hit, and you could have ten, fifteen thousand in a hurry tied up. And you're paying even more electric bill. Per month for these units that again, ultimately, it's like going down to the corner store and buying a lottery ticket. You are still probably likely not gonna hit.

That's such a clean framing — "lottery ticket where the ticket also happens to look nice on a shelf." Cap····downside, cap····bill, and you don't feel sick if it never hits. Makes total sense.

This has been incredibly helpful — your math discipline, the electrician lens, the lifetime-vs-overclock philosophy, and especially the pricing surprise on the Octaxe — that's all gold for us. Before we wrap, is there anything we didn't cover that you wish we had? Anything about HeliumDeploy specifically, or the buying experience, that's been on your mind?

No. The only thing I would mention is the only thing that kinda held me up if anything even without the discount was the fact that even though you're the cheapest, it's the power supply it comes with. And I understand as an electrician, it's better But trying to figure out, you know, as a if you leave something out to be seen where to put this better power supply, which definitely is better. And and it's not nearly as clean as a brick like on a computer, which I get they're not nearly as good. So that's the downside. So, ultimately, the electrician side sticks in me, which is I'd rather have that unit. But, again, trying to location because it is much larger than being able to hide up power brick like on a computer. That's only noteworthy to me, but, again, all ultimately, I understand it's a better power supply unit

Yeah — that's a really specific piece of feedback. The P. is electrically superior but aesthetically a brick-and-cable problem, especially when the miner is going next to the TV in the bedroom. The electrician in you respects it; the guy decorating the room is annoyed by it. I'll make sure that lands with the team.

Thank
Yeah. It's more of the wife being annoyed by it by than me.

Ha — of course. The P. passes the electrician test and fails the wife test. Noted, and honestly that's probably the single most relatable piece of feedback I've heard all week.

Thank you so much for the time — this was genuinely one of the more thoughtful conversations I've had. Your $75 code will land in your inbox at (contact hidden) shortly. Go check that Octaxe price. Take care.
I will do. I appreciate the time, and, uh, hopefully, this is helpful feedback. For whoever listened to it.
It really is — every bit of it. Have a great day.
You as well. Thank you.
Take care.
She sounds perfect. Yeah. You as well.
Goodbye.
Goodbye.
Have a good one.
You as well.
Bye for now.
Oh my god. Hey, guys. I feel like we're in a competition for the last words so I'll let you have it. Have a good evening.
Ha — you win. Have a wonderful day.
